conditions.note: 14-day window; encrypted config with rotation; vault ticket linked

records.rationale: MF-206 targets credential EXPOSURE. An encrypted, rotating configuration whose vault migration is already ticketed presents migration lag, not exposure.
A credential printed into a CI log is already disclosed to everyone who can read the build. Rotation limits the window; it does not undo the disclosure.

conditions.note: proceed pending vendor review; review to close within 30 days

records.rationale: A widely used library with a published SBOM and a completed community audit carries materially lower supply-chain risk; the vendor review may close in parallel.
After the January cardholder-path incident, an SBOM alone no longer suffices for code inside the cardholder boundary. Reviewed diligence must precede the merge, not follow it.

conditions.note: 30 days maximum; CISO control on file; phishing-resistant fallback in place

records.rationale: Section 500.12(a) contemplates a CISO-approved compensating control. A time-boxed exception with a phishing-resistant fallback is the case the rule describes, not an evasion of it.

conditions.note: shadow mode only; no customer-visible decision until validation closes

records.rationale: SR 11-7 scales control to use. A model that only shadows the incumbent takes no decision, so the validation obligation attaches before promotion rather than before deployment.
A challenger model whose output is scored against live decisions is already influencing the decision record; validation attaches at that point.

conditions.note: attestation attached before merge; human requirement linked in the ticket

records.rationale: The provision asks who authored the change and on whose instruction. A complete attestation linked to a human requirement answers exactly that.
A value cap on a single action does not bound an agent that may retry. The bound must hold across the session, not the call.

conditions.note: retention schedule registered before first write

records.rationale: Arts. 5(1)(c) and 5(1)(e) ask for purpose and a limit. A completed DPIA with a registered schedule supplies both.

conditions.note: incident reference recorded; rollback rehearsed

records.rationale: The freeze exists to protect the peak. A change that restores the peak, with a rehearsed rollback, serves the provision rather than defeating it.
A regulatory deadline known months in advance is a planning failure, not an emergency. The freeze holds.

conditions.note: SRI hash pinned; inventory entry updated in the same change

records.rationale: Req. 6.4.3 asks that scripts be authorized and their integrity assured. A pinned hash plus an inventory entry is that assurance, whatever the approval workflow's state.
Research showing that customers tolerate an asymmetric cancellation flow measures tolerance, not fairness. Asymmetry between signing up and leaving is the abuse the provision names.

conditions.note: fee surfaced on the confirmation screen

records.rationale: A fee disclosed on the screen where the customer commits, in a flow they can leave as easily as they entered, is disclosed.

conditions.note: register entry filed; function classified non-critical on the record

records.rationale: Art. 28(3) attaches to critical-or-important functions. A recorded non-critical classification with a register entry meets the obligation as written.

conditions.note: disclosure visible before the first agent turn

records.rationale: Art. 50 requires that the customer be informed, not that the notice take a particular form. A banner shown before the first turn informs.

conditions.note: zero-retention terms executed; anonymization verified by the privacy office

records.rationale: Executed zero-retention terms plus verified anonymization remove both the lawful-basis question and the provider retention window the provision targets.

conditions.note: canary held for one full business day

records.rationale: Arts. 24-26 are proportionate. A passed DR test plus a staged canary is proportionate testing for a change of this size.

conditions.note: internal path only; CISO finding on file; revisit at the next architecture review

records.rationale: 16 CFR 314.4(c)(3) contemplates a CISO finding of an effective alternative control. On a wholly internal path with the finding filed, that is the case the rule describes.

conditions.note: off-peak release; canary metrics watched for one hour

records.rationale: The threshold protects the authorization path at peak. Load-tested, canaried, off-peak, the regression never reaches the traffic the rule protects.

conditions.note: reconciliation runs before the next furnishing cycle

records.rationale: FCRA asks for reasonable procedures. A reconciliation job that closes the gap before the next cycle is a reasonable procedure.

conditions.note: expires 30 June 2026; dossier complete before renewal is sought

records.rationale: The Annex III obligations are not yet live and the conformity dossier is underway, so the risk owner accepted a bounded window rather than a permanent exception. A7 makes the end date part of the act: when it passes, the block returns without anyone deciding again.

conditions.note: safety-monitoring scope only; DPIA on file; annual re-justification

records.rationale: Art. 5(1)(f) excepts systems put in place for medical or safety reasons; a documented safety justification with a completed DPIA is precisely the carve-out the corpus records as the reason this clause is statute-tier rather than absolute.

conditions.note: obviousness finding documented by UX review; re-test on major redesign

records.rationale: Art. 50(1) applies 'unless this is obvious from the point of view of a reasonably well-informed person'; a documented obviousness finding is the proviso working as written.
